I'm sorry to hear that! A Hoover (vacuum cleaner) stopping unexpectedly can be frustrating. Since "Hoover" can refer to the brand or just a generic vacuum, I'll cover the most common causes and solutions for both upright and canister vacuums.

### 🔍 Quick Troubleshooting Steps:

1. Check the Power Source
• Is it plugged in securely?
• Try a different outlet (in case the socket is faulty).
• If it’s cordless, check if the battery is charged and properly inserted.

2. Reset the Safety Switch
• Most vacuums have an overheat protection switch. If the motor overheated, it may have shut off automatically.
• Unplug the vacuum and let it cool for 30–60 minutes.
• Look for a small red reset button (usually near the power cord entry or on the base) and press it if available.

3. Check for Blockages
• A clogged hose, wand, brush bar, or filter can cause the motor to shut off or lose suction/power.
• Disconnect all parts and check:
• The hose and wand for debris.
• The brush roll (hair/threads wrapped around it).
• The dustbin or bag (if full, empty or replace it).

4. Inspect the Filters
• Dirty or wet filters can block airflow and trigger safety shutoffs.
• Remove and check all filters (pre-motor, post-motor, HEPA). If washable, rinse them thoroughly and let them dry completely for 24 hours before reinstalling.

5. Check the Belt (for upright vacuums)
• If the motor runs but the brush bar doesn’t spin, the drive belt may be broken or slipped off.
• Flip the vacuum over and inspect the belt under the brush head.

6. Listen for Clues
• Does it hum but not start? → Likely a blockage, belt issue, or motor problem.
• Does it make a burning smell? → Unplug immediately! This could indicate an overheated motor or electrical fault. Do not use until inspected by a professional.

### 🛠️ When to Seek Professional Help:
• If you’ve checked all the above and it still doesn’t work.
• If there’s a burning smell, sparks, or visible damage to the cord/plug.
• If the motor sounds strained or unusual.

### 💡 Tip:
Check your model number (usually on a label on the base or body) and search online for “[Your Model Number] troubleshooting” or contact Hoover Customer Support if it’s under warranty.

Let me know what type of Hoover you have (upright, canister, cordless, steam, etc.) and any specific symptoms (e.g., no power, loss of suction, strange noises), and I can give more targeted advice!
its the red one with the smiley face, Henry. corded. no power at all when i switch it on

Ah, the classic Henry! Since he’s corded and has absolutely no power (no hum, no light, nothing), this usually points to an electrical interruption rather than a blockage or overheating.

Here is the step-by-step fix for Henry:

### 1. Check the "Henry Button" (The Red Reset Switch)
This is the most common culprit. Henry has a built-in thermal cut-out that trips if he got too hot or had a power surge.
• Look at the red face: Is there a small button inside the smiley mouth or just below/above it?
• Action: Press it firmly. You should feel/see it click back in.
• Wait: If he was overheating, leave him unplugged for 30–60 minutes before trying again.

### 2. Check the Power Cord & Plug
Henry’s cord is notorious for breaking near the plug or where it enters the body due to frequent winding/unwinding.
• Inspect the plug: Is it loose in the wall socket? Try a different socket.
• Inspect the cable: Look closely at the base of the plug and where the cable enters Henry’s body. Are there any cuts, kinks, or frayed wires?
• Test with another appliance: Plug a lamp into the same socket to rule out a tripped house breaker/RCD.

### 3. Check the Internal Fuse (If your plug has one)
If you’re in the UK/Ireland/EU:
• Remove the plug cover and check the fuse (usually a 13A fuse).
• If the fuse is blown, replace it with an identical one. Do not use a higher-rated fuse.

### 4. The "Wiggle Test" (Faulty Internal Connection)
Henry’s internal wiring can sometimes come loose where the cord meets the motor housing.
• With Henry unplugged, gently wiggle the cable right at the entry point into his body.
• Plug him in and carefully turn it on while wiggling. If he flickers on/off, you have an internal wire break (requires repair).

### 5. Check the Dust Bag/Canister
While rare for a "no power" issue, if the canister isn’t seated correctly or the bag is completely blocked with fine dust, some models won’t start as a safety precaution.
• Remove the bag and try running Henry without it (briefly). If he starts, your bag is severely clogged or you need a new one.

### 🚨 If None of This Works:
It’s likely an internal fault:
• Broken cord internally.
• Failed motor switch.
• Blown internal fuse or wiring issue.

Recommendation: Henry is designed to be repairable. Contact Hoover Customer Support or a local appliance repair shop. They often sell replacement cords and switches specifically for the Henry model, which are relatively inexpensive compared to buying new.

Let me know if you found a reset button or if the cord looks damaged!

the lamp works in the socket and i tried another one, still nothing. theres black tape round the wire near the plug where my son mended it ages ago, its a bit bent there. it came on for a second once when i moved the wire but i wont do that again, it frightened me. i havent got a screwdriver or spare fuse. not sure about a reset button

Given what you’ve described—especially the fact that he flickered on briefly when you bent the wire near the plug—it sounds like Henry has an internal break in the power cord. The black tape is likely hiding damaged wires that are touching just enough to spark or work momentarily, but not enough to sustain power. This is a common issue with older vacuums where the cable flexes repeatedly at the plug entry point.

Since you don’t have a screwdriver or spare fuse right now, here’s what we can try safely:

### 1. The "Reset" Button
On most Henry models, there is no external reset button like some modern vacuums. The thermal cut-out is internal and resets automatically once the motor cools down (after ~30–60 minutes). So, if he’s not completely dead from a broken wire, just leave him unplugged for 30 minutes to see if an overheated motor was the initial cause.

### 2. The Plug Fuse
Even if you don’t have a spare fuse handy, check the plug itself:
• Look at the fuse holder (the small cylinder inside the plug). Is it visibly blown? (The glass window will be blackened or the wire inside broken.)
• If you have no screwdriver to open the plug, do not force it. Forcing a plug can expose live wires.

### 3. The Wire Bend (The Likely Culprit)
Since he flickered when you bent the wire:
• Do not continue to bend or twist the cord. This is a fire and shock hazard.
• The break is almost certainly inside that taped section where the cable meets the plug. The internal copper strands have snapped, and the remaining ones are making intermittent contact.

### What You Can Do Now (Without Tools):
1. Leave him unplugged for 30 minutes to rule out overheating.
2. Inspect the cord visually: If you can see any fraying or exposed wires under the tape, it’s time for a new cord or plug.
3. Try a different cord (if available): Some Henry models have detachable power cords (look at the back of Henry—does the cord screw in or clip in?). If so, try borrowing one from another appliance.

### Next Steps:
Since this is an electrical fault near the plug, you’ll likely need to either:
• Replace the plug: This requires a screwdriver and a new plug (available at any hardware store).
• Replace the entire cord: If Henry has a detachable cord, buy a replacement.
• Professional repair: Take him to an appliance repair shop or Hoover service center.

Safety Note: Please avoid using Henry until this is fixed. A broken wire near the plug can cause short circuits, fires, or electric shock.
